subject: GATE Computer Science and Information Technology

topics: Verbal Aptitude: grammar, vocabulary, reading comprehension, analogies
Quantitative Aptitude: arithmetic, percentages, ratios, data interpretation, mensuration
Analytical Aptitude: logic, deduction, relationships, seating arrangements, counting
Spatial Aptitude: shapes, rotation, mirror images, paper folding, patterns
Sets, relations, functions, partial orders and lattices
Combinatorics: counting, recurrence relations, generating functions
Random variables and distributions: uniform, normal, exponential, Poisson, binomial
Mean, median, mode and standard deviation
Number representations and computer arithmetic: fixed and floating point
Memory hierarchy: cache, main memory and secondary storage
I/O interface: interrupt and DMA mode
Trees, binary search trees and binary heaps
Asymptotic worst case time and space complexity
Graph traversals, minimum spanning trees and shortest paths
Regular and context-free languages, pumping lemma
Local optimisation, data flow analysis: constant propagation, liveness, common subexpression elimination
Inter-process communication, concurrency and synchronization: semaphores, locks
Memory management and virtual memory: paging, page replacement
Relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL
Integrity constraints and normal forms: functional dependencies, BCNF, 3NF
File organization and indexing: B and B+ trees
Transactions and concurrency control: serializability, locking
Layering: OSI and TCP/IP protocol stacks
Packet, circuit and virtual circuit switching
Data link layer: framing, error detection, MAC, Ethernet bridging
Routing protocols: shortest path, flooding, distance vector, link state
IP addressing: IPv4, CIDR, subnetting, fragmentation, ARP, DHCP, ICMP, NAT
Transport layer: flow control and congestion control, UDP, TCP, sockets
Application layer protocols: DNS, SMTP, HTTP, FTP, Email
